   CALL TO ORDER

  Pu

 1. PUBLIC COMMENT

 2. NEW BUSINESS

  A. 10-POINT PLAN FOR RECOVERY, RESILIENCY, AND REINVESTMENT
  ESTABLISHING PROGRAMS WITH CDBG SUPPLEMENTAL FUNDING

  On May 19, 2020, Economic Development staff presented a 10-Point Plan for
  Recovery, Resiliency, and Reinvestment to help mitigate the financial impacts of
  the novel coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19). The 10-Point Plan provided
  different program ideas to support the business community. Staff also presented
  several options for use of the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
  supplemental funding received through the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, And
  Economic Security Act (CARES Act). City Council requested that staff return with
  more information regarding certain proposed programs and potential funding
  allocations to benefit both residents and businesses.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the allocation $186,148 of CDBG
  supplemental funding to the Housing Relief Program, Small Business Grant
  Program, and Senior Meal Program, direct staff to administer the programs, and
  increase the expenditure appropriation and revenue accounts accordingly in
  Fund 185.

  B. FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 OPERATING BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT
  PROGRAM

  A public hearing was held at the regular City Council meeting of June 2, 2020 to
  consider adoption of Proposed Budget for FY 2020-21. Upon closing the public
  hearing, the City Council discussed the budget and made recommendations for
  further reductions. The item was then continued to this meeting to allow staff the
  opportunity to research issues raised. This report continues the discussion from
  June 2, 2020 regarding the FY 2020-21 Proposed Budget and addresses
  comments raised by the Council.

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – June 9, 2020  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council provide direction to staff for any
  amendments to the Proposed Budget for FY 2020-21.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 20-31 – A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF SAN GABRIEL RESPONDING TO RECENT DEMONSTRATIONS
  FOLLOWING THE DEATH OF GEORGE FLOYD, AND STATING THE CITY'S
  SUPPORT FOR (A) THE PEACEFUL ASSEMBLY OF PERSONS PROTESTING
  AND COMMUNICATING FOLLOWING THE EVENTS (B) THE REVIEW OF
  PRACTICES AND POLICIES OF LAW ENFORCEMENT

  The City Council will consider the adoption of Resolution No. 20-31, a Resolution
  responding to recent demonstrations following the death of George Floyd. The
  resolution proclaims the City’s support for the peaceful assembly of persons
  protesting and communicating following the events and the review of practices
  and policies of law enforcement.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Resolution No. 20-31.

  3. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, June 16, 2020 at
  6:30 p.m. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF JUNE 9, 2020
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
5:04 P.M. on Tuesday, June 9, 2020, with all Council Members and staff participating by
teleconference.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto; City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux;  Assistant  City  Manager/Community
  Development Director Arminé Chaparyan, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Dr. Chastity Jennings-Nuñez provided comments regarding the Justice for George
  Floyd Briefing presented at the June 2, 2020 Regular City Council meeting.

2. NEW BUSINESS

  A. 10-POINT PLAN FOR RECOVERY, RESILIENCY, AND REINVESTMENT
  ESTABLISHING PROGRAMS WITH CDBG SUPPLEMENTAL FUNDING

  The staff report was presented by Management Assistant Claudia Gelin.

  Clarification discussion included staff hours and cost for staff to administrate the
  program; using a consultant would mean less money for residents or businesses;
  how staff determined proposed allocations; business grants for Asian Youth Center
  (AYC) and small businesses; and staff’s capacity to administer the program.

  An un-named commenter provided questions regarding housing grants.

  Sean McMorris, resident, provided comments in support of the staff
  recommendation and commended the Asian Youth Center for doing a wonderful
  job in the community.

CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 4  June 9, 2020
   Discussion included state and federal funds that may be available; paying grant
  monies directly to the landlord rather than the tenant; mask and sanitizer
  donations received and requested; application process for grants and timing for
  the program; community spending coupon program; priority for businesses to
  open; a lottery to choose grant recipients; tracking mechanism for grant criteria
  adherence; and outreach suggestions.

  A motion was made by Council Member Harrington, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao,
  to approve the allocation of $186,148 in CDBG supplemental funding to the
  Housing Relief Program, Small Business Grant Program, and Senior Meal Program,
  direct staff to administer the programs, and increase the expenditure appropriation
  and revenue accounts accordingly in Fund 185.

  Motion approved New Business Item 2A as presented by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 OPERATING BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT
  PROGRAM

  The staff report was presented by Management Specialist Julia James.

  Clarifying discussion included the value of membership in various regional
  organizations.

  The following provided comments in support of reducing funding for the Police
  Department in favor of various other options: Alejandra Benavides; Stacy Ruiz;
  Emily Scannell, resident; Gabriel Frank-McPheter, Gabrielino High School student
  and June 6th protest organizer; Chloe Tan, resident; Cathy Nguyen, resident;
  Andrew Gamba, resident; Jorge De La Cruz, resident; Bianca Lua, resident; Andrew
  Phu, resident; Christopher Rivera, resident; Winston Smith, resident; Emma Sieh,
  resident; Melanie Pham, resident; Cindy Kreeck; Nathan Mendoza, resident; Alvin
  Gip, resident; Samantha del Pozo, resident; Theresa Thuy, resident; Alden Do,
  resident; Elizabeth Campos, resident; Joshua Raymundo; Bellini Martinez, resident;
  Austin Raymundo, resident; Nathan Villavicenico, resident; Angelica Lujan, resident;
  Joyce Truong; Arturo Quinonez, resident; Tamara Dang, resident; Neil McMaster,
  resident; Jessica Dong, resident; Jerry Kong, resident; Vivian Sam, resident and prior
  student of the SGUSD; Meggie Nguyen, resident; Rosalynn Luong, resident; and
  Brinca Siow, resident.

  The following provided comments in opposition to reducing funding for the Police
  Department: Christine Tureaud; Lynn Snowden, resident; Sue Fitzsimmons;
  Charmaine Liccardi, resident; Bradford Snowden; Maureen Dizon, resident; and
  Patty Rodriguez, resident.

  Michael Schutz, resident, provided comments in opposition to funding the San
  Gabriel Chamber of Commerce.

  Harry Baldwin and Mary Cammarano, former San Gabriel City Council Members.
  provided comments in support of funding membership for the League of California
  Cities, National League of Cities, San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments
  (SGVCOG) and the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG).

CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 4  June 9, 2020
   Chasity Jennings-Nuñez provided comments requesting that funding for the Police
  Department be maintained and not increased, the Community Services budget not
  be decreased, administrative costs be cut, and that in-person summer camps and
  programs be allowed to open.

  Ethan Tan provided comments requesting that the percentage of budget allocation
  for the Police, Community Services and Public Works Departments be reformulated
  in favor of the latter two departments.

  Kevin Diep, resident, provided questions regarding the stimulus package.

  Ryan Qu, resident, provided comments requesting an increase in funding for the
  Police Department.

  Discussion included: Police Department funding allocation; clarification that the
  Police Department is already working with mental health professionals; Council’s
  responsibility to protect the citizens in relation to reducing the Police Department
  budget; the value of membership in various regional organizations and associated
  agreements; funding related to the Historic Preservation Ordinance; timing and
  facilitation for a new strategic plan; methodology for budget cuts if they are
  needed; reducing the travel and conference budget for council members;
  conversations with the community about Police funding and related issues; cultural
  changes in the organization that have already occurred; budget challenges due to
  COVID-19; the Budget as a planning document requiring periodic adjustments;
  value of community engagement in revising City organizational structure and the
  timing required for adopting this Budget; lack of discretionary funds; and engaging
  more with the community.

  There was a majority of the Council in agreement to reduce the individual council
  member travel and conference budget to $3000 each; remove the proposed
  amount for a new strategic plan; retain the funding for memberships in various
  regional organizations; and retain the proposed amount for the Historic
  Preservation Ordinance.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to make
  the following changes to the proposed budget:
  1. Reduce the individual Council Member travel and conference budget to
  $3000 each; and
  2. Remove the amount proposed for a new strategic plan.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:
  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 20-31 – A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF SAN GABRIEL RESPONDING TO RECENT DEMONSTRATIONS FOLLOWING
  THE DEATH OF GEORGE FLOYD, AND STATING THE CITY'S SUPPORT FOR (A)
  THE  PEACEFUL  ASSEMBLY  OF  PERSONS  PROTESTING  AND
  COMMUNICATING FOLLOWING THE EVENTS, AND (B) THE REVIEW OF
  PRACTICES AND POLICIES OF LAW ENFORCEMENT

  Mayor Menchaca presented the agenda report.
